The *Phārusaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* is a short verse text located in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. As with other poems in this section, it recounts the past meritorious karmic deed of an elder—here involving the offering of a *phārusa* fruit—and its subsequent spiritual rewards [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations across five languages [SuttaCentral]. Passages in secondary scholarship citing "Apadāna 387" refer to the *Pubbakammapiloti-apadāna* according to the Pali Text Society edition's numbering system rather than this text.

According to DharmaNexus, the text exhibits extensive formulaic text reuse internally within the Pali canon and its commentaries, sharing 120 matching passages with 46 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest matches occur with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, 21 matches) and a network of structurally parallel fruit-offering poems in the *Therāpadāna*, such as *Pādaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 507), *Nāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 517), *Kapitthaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 514), and adjacent texts including *Pilakkhaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 386) and *Kāsumāriphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 382) [DharmaNexus].
